      "value": 59.0,

      "measures": "share of articles that stated the hypothesis or objective of the study and the number and characteristics of the animals used",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",
      "species": [],
      "n": 271,
      "n_counts": "articles assessed",
      "verbatim": "The survey, commissioned by the National Centre for the Replacement, Refinement and Reduction of Animals in Research (NC3Rs), a UK Government-sponsored scientific organisation, found that only 59% of the 271 randomly chosen articles assessed stated the hypothesis or objective of the study and the number and characteristics of the animals used (i.e., species/strain, sex and age/weight)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "percentage of papers not reporting randomisation",
      "value": 87.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of papers that did not report using randomisation to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "papers",
      "verbatim": "Most of the papers surveyed did not report using randomisation (87%) or blinding (86%) to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "percentage of papers not reporting blinding",
      "value": 86.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of papers that did not report using blinding to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "papers",
      "verbatim": "Most of the papers surveyed did not report using randomisation (87%) or blinding (86%) to reduce bias in animal selection and outcome assessment."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "percentage of publications fully describing statistical methods and presenting results with a measure of precision or variability",
      "value": 70.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of publications that used statistical methods and fully described them and presented the results with a measure of precision or variability",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "publications that used statistical methods",
      "verbatim": "Only 70% of the publications that used statistical methods fully described them and presented the results with a measure of precision or variability."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "percentage of articles not reporting the number of animals used",
      "value": 4.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of articles that did not report the number of animals used anywhere in the methods or the results sections",
      "compared": "animal research articles vs. reporting requirements",
      "species": [],
      "n": 271,
      "n_counts": "journal articles assessed",
      "verbatim": "Our review found that 4% of the 271 journal articles assessed did not report the number of animals used anywhere in the methods or the results sections."
    }
  ],
  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study assessed the reporting quality of bioscience research articles, particularly those involving animal research, and developed guidelines (ARRIVE) to improve this reporting.",
  "what_it_found": "A significant proportion of bioscience research articles, especially those using animals, suffer from inadequate reporting of methods and results, hindering their utility and potentially leading to research waste.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "In many cases, the publications themselves are not “fit for purpose,” meaning that incomplete reporting of relevant information effectively renders many publications of limited value as instruments to inform policy or clinical and scientific practice.",
      "topic": "Publication Value"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Failure to describe research methods and to report results appropriately therefore has potential scientific, ethical and economic implications for the entire research process and the reputation of those involved in it.",
      "topic": "Reporting Implications"
    },
    {
      "quote": "The largest and most comprehensive review of published animal research undertaken to date, to our knowledge, has highlighted serious omissions in the way research using animals is reported.",
      "topic": "Animal Research Omissions"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Only 70% of the publications that used statistical methods fully described them and presented the results with a measure of precision or variability.",
      "topic": "Statistical Reporting"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Most bioscience journals currently provide little or no guidance on what information to report when describing animal research.",
      "topic": "Journal Guidance"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Well-designed and -reported animal studies are the essential building blocks from which such a systematic review is constructed.",
      "topic": "Study Building Blocks"
    }
  ]
}
